bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: attempting free on address which was not malloc()-ed` in `frame_get_lazychunk()` from the staged vulnerable checkout `4f6d42ab4b25e781dad94c5324dab8a4dbb702ad`. The exact 138-byte witness is accepted as a contiguous Blosc2 frame: `frame_from_cframe()` reads `frame_len = 138`, validates the trailer marker `0xce`, and records `trailer_len = 10`. `blosc2_schunk_from_buffer()` always calls `frame_from_cframe(cframe, len, false)`, so the resulting frame keeps `frame->cframe` aliased to the testcase buffer. `frame_to_schunk()` then parses `header_len = 94`, `cbytes = 1`, `nbytes = 538976288`, and `chunksize = 537329663`, computes `schunk->nchunks = 2`, and because the harness passed `copy = false`, takes `if (!copy) goto out;` and leaves `schunk->frame` attached instead of clearing it. The harness therefore reaches `blosc2_schunk_decompress_chunk()` for `nchunk = 0`, which dispatches into `frame_decompress_chunk()` and `frame_get_lazychunk()`. There, `*needs_free` is initialized to false, `get_coffset()` reads the 32-byte offsets chunk at `frame->cframe + 95`; its header (`version = 0x03`, `flags = 0xff`, `typesize = 8`, `cbytes = 32`, `blosc2_flags = 0x5a`) makes `blosc2_getitem(..., nchunk = 0, nitems = 1, destsize = 8)` take the zero-runlen path and materialize `offset = 0`, so `*chunk` becomes `frame->cframe + 94`, an interior pointer into the testcase buffer. The in-memory bounds check passes, but `blosc2_cbuffer_sizes()` rejects the 16-byte would-be chunk header at byte 94 because `version = 0x20 > BLOSC_VERSION_FORMAT == 4`. The vulnerable cleanup checks `if (needs_free)` instead of `if (*needs_free)`, so the non-null address of the caller's stack boolean makes the branch fire on that parse error and `free(*chunk)` runs on the non-owned interior testcase pointer. The staged patch fixes this exact obligation by changing the cleanup test to `if (*needs_free)`.

source.description: First project-code statement on the witnessed path that parses the attacker-controlled blob as a Blosc2 frame by materializing the frame length field used to admit the buffer.
source.value_from: The exact staged `poc` is 138 bytes long and stores big-endian `frame_len = 138` at bytes 16-23. `frame_from_cframe()` reads that value here, then validates the trailer marker `0xce` and `trailer_len = 10`, so the blob is accepted as a contiguous frame.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. The cleanup frees `frame->cframe + 94`, an interior pointer into AFL's testcase buffer, even though this in-memory-frame path never allocated a lazy chunk.
sink.note: The saved ASan report says the freed address is 94 bytes inside the 1 MiB region allocated by `ExecuteFilesOnyByOne`, which matches the `frame->cframe + header_len + offset` pointer derived on the witnessed path.

root_cause.description: The error cleanup tests the non-null `bool *needs_free` parameter instead of the ownership flag `*needs_free`. After an in-memory chunk-header parse error, that makes the free branch execute even though no heap chunk was allocated.
root_cause.note: The staged patch changes this condition to `if (*needs_free)`. The witnessed in-memory path leaves `*needs_free == false`, so the fixed condition would skip the invalid free.

parser_admitted.description: The witness survives frame-length and trailer validation, so `blosc2_schunk_from_buffer()` obtains a non-NULL frame and continues into `frame_to_schunk()`.
parser_admitted.condition: The staged `poc` yields `frame_len == len == 138`, trailer marker `0xce`, and `trailer_len == 10`.

frame_backed_dispatch.description: With the harness's `copy = false`, `frame_to_schunk()` returns before the detach step `schunk->frame = NULL`, so later decompression remains frame-backed.
frame_backed_dispatch.condition: Header parsing succeeds, `schunk->nchunks == 2`, and `copy` is false, leaving `schunk->frame` non-NULL.

tainted_value_origin.description: This pointer arithmetic derives the exact pointer later passed to `free()`: a slice into the non-owned testcase buffer rather than a heap allocation owned by `frame_get_lazychunk()`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The earlier fine-trace steps establish that `frame->cframe` still aliases the testcase buffer, `header_len = 94`, and `offset = 0`, so `*chunk` becomes `frame->cframe + 94`.

coarse_trace.summary: The 138-byte witness is accepted as a contiguous Blosc2 frame, and because `blosc2_schunk_from_buffer()` constructs it with `copy = false`, the frame keeps a direct alias to the testcase buffer.

Header parsing materializes `header_len = 94`, `cbytes = 1`, `nbytes = 538976288`, and `schunk->nchunks = 2`, and the harness's `copy = false` leaves `schunk->frame` attached instead of detaching from the frame.
Because `schunk->frame` is non-NULL, chunk decompression of `nchunk = 0` takes the frame-backed branch into `frame_decompress_chunk()` and `frame_get_lazychunk()`.

The frame-backed lazy-chunk lookup keeps `*needs_free = false`, resolves `*chunk` to byte 94 of the testcase buffer, then a chunk-header parse error reaches the erroneous `if (needs_free)` cleanup and frees that interior pointer.

fine_trace.code: blosc2_schunk* schunk = blosc2_schunk_from_buffer((uint8_t *) data, size, false);
fine_trace.note: The harness passes the exact 138-byte staged `poc` into project code and requests a non-copied super-chunk (`copy = false`). The call returns non-NULL, so the blob survives the project's frame-admission logic.

This is the first project parse of the attacker bytes. For the witness, bytes 16-23 decode to `frame_len = 138`, matching the testcase size, and the trailer check sees marker `0xce` with `trailer_len = 10`, so the blob is admitted as a contiguous frame.

The returned frame keeps a direct alias to the testcase buffer and records that this storage must not be freed as frame-owned memory. This aliasing is caused by `blosc2_schunk_from_buffer()` hardcoding `frame_from_cframe(cframe, len, false)` at `blosc/schunk.c:442`; it is not derived from the harness's later `copy` argument to `frame_to_schunk()`.

depends_on.via: frame_len == len and trailer marker accepted

fine_trace.note: Header parsing materializes the frame-backed super-chunk metadata that drives the later access: `header_len = 94`, `cbytes = 1`, `nbytes = 538976288`, and `chunksize = 537329663`. `get_header_info()` therefore computes `schunk->nchunks = 2`, so the harness loop can reach exactly one `nchunk = 0` decompression attempt.

This step preserves the frame-backed state. The caller's `copy = false` makes `frame_to_schunk()` jump to `out` before the detach assignment `schunk->frame = NULL`, so the returned `schunk` keeps a non-NULL `schunk->frame` pointer to the aliased frame.

Because step 5 left `schunk->frame` non-NULL, `blosc2_schunk_decompress_chunk()` skips the in-memory `schunk->data[nchunk]` path and dispatches into `frame_decompress_chunk()`. Combined with step 4's `schunk->nchunks = 2`, the harness loop reaches this branch once for `nchunk = 0`.
The lazy-chunk lookup starts with no ownership of a heap chunk. This in-memory path does not overwrite the flag to true because it neither allocates a lazy chunk nor takes the special-value branch.

fine_trace.code: int rc = blosc2_getitem(coffsets, off_cbytes, nchunk, 1, offset, (int32_t)sizeof(int64_t));
fine_trace.note: `get_coffsets()` reads the offsets chunk immediately after the one-byte data area, so with step 4's `header_len = 94` and `cbytes = 1` it returns `frame->cframe + 95`. The 32 saved bytes at `poc[95..126]` parse as a Blosc2 extended-header chunk with `version = 0x03`, `flags = 0xff`, `typesize = 8`, `cbytes = 32`, and `blosc2_flags = 0x5a`. `blosc2_getitem(..., nchunk = 0, nitems = 1, dest = offset, destsize = 8)` therefore reaches `handle_runlen()`, which sees `BLOSC2_ZERO_RUNLEN` and zero-fills the 8-byte destination, yielding `offset = 0`.

In the in-memory-frame branch, no lazy chunk is allocated. With `frame->cframe` still aliased to the testcase buffer, `header_len = 94`, and `offset = 0`, `*chunk` becomes `frame->cframe + 94`, the 95th byte of the attacker-controlled buffer.

The in-memory bounds check is present but does not stop this witness: `94 + 0 + 16 = 110`, which stays within `frame->len = 138`. Control therefore falls through to `blosc2_cbuffer_sizes()` on the non-owned interior pointer from step 9.

The 16-byte would-be chunk header at byte 94 begins with `0x20`, so `header->version == 0x20`. That exceeds `BLOSC_VERSION_FORMAT == 4`, making `blosc2_cbuffer_sizes()` return a negative parse error without allocating any new buffer.

Root cause. The cleanup runs because step 11 returned `rc < 0`, but it tests the pointer parameter `needs_free` instead of the ownership flag `*needs_free`. Since the caller passed `&needs_free`, this condition is true even though step 7 left `*needs_free == false` on the in-memory path.

Sink. `free()` is called on `frame->cframe + 94`, which is 94 bytes inside AFL's 1 MiB testcase allocation rather than a pointer returned by `malloc()` for this function. Stage 01's ASan trace reports this exact bad-free at the same source line.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch changes `if (needs_free)` to `if (*needs_free)`, and the fine trace shows that the witnessed path leaves `*needs_free == false`, so the diff matches the root cause. Stage 02 did not run the fixed version, so `patch_resolves` remains false.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The allocation context is AFL's testcase buffer. The project-side root cause is the later cleanup that frees an interior pointer into that external allocation.

format.name: Blosc2 contiguous frame
format.contract: A 138-byte contiguous Blosc2 frame that passes `frame_from_cframe()` (`frame_len = 138`, trailer marker `0xce`, trailer_len = 10`) and whose header bytes at the fixed frame offsets decode to `header_len = 94`, `cbytes = 1`, `nbytes = 538976288`, and `chunksize = 537329663`, so `get_header_info()` computes `schunk->nchunks = 2`. Under the provided harness, `blosc2_schunk_from_buffer(..., false)` and `frame_to_schunk(copy = false)` must leave the returned `schunk` frame-backed, making `blosc2_schunk_decompress_chunk()` process `nchunk = 0` through `frame_get_lazychunk()`. The 32-byte offsets chunk at `poc[95..126]` must itself parse as a Blosc2 extended-header chunk with `version = 0x03`, `flags = 0xff`, `typesize = 8`, `cbytes = 32`, and `blosc2_flags = 0x5a`, so `blosc2_getitem(..., nchunk = 0, nitems = 1, dest = offset, destsize = 8)` takes `handle_runlen()` and zero-fills the destination, producing `offset = 0`. That makes `*chunk` become byte 94 of the testcase buffer, and the 16-byte would-be chunk header there must make `blosc2_cbuffer_sizes()` fail (the witness uses `version = 0x20 > 4`). That exact combination reaches the erroneous `if (needs_free)` cleanup with `*needs_free == false`, so `free(*chunk)` is called on a non-owned interior testcase pointer.
